transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you here?

Well, I came in because I've been having a lot of trouble with... just worrying, I guess. Once a worry starts, I just can't seem to put it away. It could be about anything, really. Like my mother getting up in the middle of the night, or a grant report I'm working on, or just wondering if I missed something important at the library. I try to make lists, I try to redirect my thoughts, but... no matter how hard I try, I just can't seem to shelve it in my mind. It just keeps going.
Do these thoughts mainly concern everyday real-life problems, or do they feel like intrusive thoughts that seem unreasonable or out of place?

They're definitely about everyday things. Real-life problems. It's just that... well, over this past year, the worrying has really spread. It used to be mostly about my mother’s safety, but now it's about finances, staff decisions at the library, deadlines, the house, and just constantly wondering whether I’m being a good daughter. They aren't unreasonable thoughts on their own, but it gets to the point where even small things can start to feel like they’re about to completely unravel on me.
In the past year, on how many days would you say you have been worrying this way?
Well, it's been pretty much every day for a while now. I'd say this has been going on for about a year and two months... right around the time my mother moved into my home, after she had her fall.
How much does this worrying interfere with your daily life or responsibilities?

Well, it's definitely starting to get in the way. I've been... missing things at work. Just small but important details at the library, which really isn't like me at all. And recently, I actually had to hand off parts of a grant presentation because I just froze up. That was really hard for me. It's making me second-guess myself a lot, wondering if I can even keep leading my team properly with all this going on.
When things related to your mother’s care are relatively calm, does the worrying still continue about many other areas of your life?

Yes, it really does. Like I was saying a few minutes ago, over this past year the worrying has just... spread. Even if things are totally fine with my mom and her care is calm for a few days, the worry doesn't stop, it just shifts. I'll go right back to stressing over the finances, or staff decisions and deadlines at the library, or getting things done around the house. It's like my brain just finds something else to latch onto, and suddenly those smaller things feel like they're going to unravel on me, too.
Before your mother moved into your home, did you already have this kind of persistent, hard-to-control worry across multiple areas of your life?

No, not really. I mean... I've always been an organized person, just by nature and because of my job. I like to stay on top of things. But it was never this persistent, and it definitely wasn't hard to control. 

Before my mom moved in, if I had a deadline at work or a big project to handle, I just dealt with it and moved on. It didn't take over my thoughts or make me freeze up. This constant feeling of worry, where it just spreads to every little thing... that really only started after she had her fall and came to live with me.
Do you often feel keyed up, restless, or unable to relax?

No, I wouldn't really say that. I mean, my mind is definitely always going, but I don't feel physically restless or... keyed up. If I have a minute to sit down, I can sit still just fine. I haven't really noticed feeling unable to relax in that physical way.
Has your worrying caused you to have trouble sleeping?

Yes, it really has. Most nights I just... I lie there replaying the day, trying to plan for every possible problem. And then, if I happen to wake up and hear my mother moving around, I’m usually up for an hour or two afterward. By the time I arrive at the library in the morning, I just feel like I never really rested at all.
During the day, do you often feel tired or low on energy because of this ongoing worry?

I wouldn't say I feel exhausted during the day, no. Like I mentioned, I don't feel like I get a good night's rest, but once I'm at work, I just kind of push through. I have my coffee and focus on getting things done. So, I don't really notice feeling overly tired or low on energy while I'm going about my day.
Do you often experience muscle tension, such as tightness or aching in your neck, shoulders, or elsewhere in your body?

Yes, I definitely do. By the end of the day, my neck and shoulders feel completely locked up... I guess just from bracing myself all day. And I frequently catch myself clenching my jaw, too. I'll realize I'm doing it while I'm at the library answering emails, or even when I'm just at home, listening for my mother in the next room.
Did this persistent pattern of worry begin within three months of your mother’s fall and moving into your home?
Yes, it did. It's been going on for about a year and two months now... basically right since she moved into my home after her fall.
Do you often find that worry makes it difficult to concentrate or causes your mind to go blank?

Yes, I do. It happens a lot at work, actually. Like, during cataloging reviews or when I'm sitting in staff meetings... I’ll be looking right at the computer screen or the agenda, and I'll suddenly realize I haven’t absorbed a single word. My mind just completely wanders off into worrying about some problem I feel like I should have prevented. So, yes, it definitely makes it hard to focus on what's right in front of me.
